sn12.18:1.2: Now the wanderer Timbaruka came up to the Exalted One and greeted him;
sn12.18:1.3: and when compliments of friendship and courtesy had been exchanged, he sat down at one side. So seated he spoke thus to the Exalted One:
sn12.18:2.1: “Now then, Master Gotama, is pleasure and pain brought about by one's self?”
sn12.18:2.2: “Not so, Timbaruka,” said the Exalted One.
sn12.18:2.3: “Well then, are they brought about by another?”
sn12.18:2.4: “Not so, Timbaruka,” said the Exalted One.
sn12.18:2.5: “Well then, are they brought about by both one's self and another?”
sn12.18:2.7: “But then, are they brought about neither by one's self nor by another, but by chance?”
sn12.18:2.9: “How then, Master Gotama, is there no such thing as pleasure or pain?”
sn12.18:2.10: “No, Timbaruka, there is pleasure and pain.”
sn12.18:2.12: “Is it then that Master Gotama neither knows nor sees pleasure and pain?”
sn12.18:2.13: “No, Timbaruka, I am not one who knows not pleasure and pain, nor sees them.
sn12.18:3.1: “How now, Master Gotama: to all my questions you have said, 'not so, Timbaruka.'
sn12.18:3.5: And, being asked as to the existence of pleasure and pain, you affirm they are, and are known and seen by you.
sn12.18:3.10: Declare to me then, Master Gotama, the truth about pleasure and pain.
sn12.18:3.11: Teach me, Master Gotama, the truth about pleasure and pain.”
sn12.18:4.1: “The experience and he who experiences hereafter are one and the same: this, Timbaruka, which you at first called 'pleasure and pain brought about by one's self' — I declare this is not so.
sn12.18:4.2: The experience and he who experiences hereafter are different one from the other: this, Timbaruka, which by one smitten by the after-experience is called 'pleasure and pain brought about by another' — I declare this is not so.
sn12.18:4.3: To you, Timbaruka, the Tathagata, not approaching either extreme, teaches the Dhamma by the middle way:
sn12.18:4.4: ‘Conditioned by ignorance activities come to pass,
sn12.18:4.5: by activities consciousness, and so on.
sn12.18:4.6: Such is the arising of this entire mass of ill.
sn12.18:4.7: But through the utter fading away and ceasing of ignorance comes ceasing of activities,
sn12.18:4.8: through ceasing of activities ceasing of consciousness, and so on.
sn12.18:4.9: Such is the ceasing of this entire mass of ill.’”
sn12.18:5.1: When this had been said, Timbaruka, the Wanderer, spoke thus to the Exalted One:
sn12.18:5.3: I, even I, lord, take myself to the Exalted One as my refuge, to the Norm and to the Order.
sn12.18:5.4: May Master Gotama accept me as a follower, as one who from this day forth, as long as life lasts, has taken his refuge therein!”
